drawings.description: sphère vue en perspective ; sur l'équateur, trois points marqués (ronds pleins), chacun entouré d'un petit cercle portant deux sommets $R_i^{\omega}$, $R_i^{\omega'}$ ($i = 0, 1, \infty$), reliés par les arcs $a_i^{\omega}$, $a_i^{\omega'}$ ; les sommets voisins de deux points différents sont reliés par les flèches $b_0^{\omega}$, $b_1^{\omega}$ (lecture douteuse), $b_\infty^{\omega}$. Légende : $\mathrm{I}_J$.
drawings.kind: sphere with marked points, small circles and arrows
drawings.notes: Sphere outline and equator in pencil; the three marked points (big dots) on the equator, each in a small oriented circle with two vertices R_i^omega, R_i^omega'. Arrows b along the equator between the circles. The label of the right-hand b arrow is overinked; it is placed as the transcription reads it (b_1^omega, doubtful). The point near the north pole is drawn.

drawings.description: même sphère que p.~23, à laquelle s'ajoutent sur l'équateur trois nouveaux sommets $Q_0$, $Q_1$, $Q_\infty$ et des arcs $c_i^{\pm}$ qui les relient aux sommets $R^{\pm}$ voisins. Légende : $\mathrm{II}_J$.
drawings.kind: sphere with marked points, small circles and arrows
drawings.notes: As 02-1 with the signs +/- for omega, omega'; the new vertices Q_0, Q_1, Q_infty on the equator and the arrows c_i^+- joining them to the R. The legend II_J (below-left of the sphere) is text, not drawn. Q_1 sits at the left end of the equator, its label being c_1^+ there.

drawings.description: à droite : petit schéma de $\tilde a_i^{\omega}$, chemin de $Q_{\omega i}$ à $Q_{\omega' i}$ passant par $(c^{\omega}_{\omega i})^{-1}$, l'arc $a_i^{\omega}$ entre $R_i^{\omega}$ et $R_i^{\omega'}$, puis $c^{\omega'}_{\omega' i}$ ; une première version, au-dessous, est rayée. Dans la marge gauche, un croquis analogue, en partie rayé.
drawings.kind: path diagram (composite arc)
drawings.notes: Right: the path as he drew it, from right to left: the arrow c^{omega'}_{omega' i} from Q_{omega' i} to the right end R_i^omega of the arc, the arc a_i^omega looping above (arrowhead at its left end), and the arrow (c^omega_{omega i})^{-1} from the left end of the arc to Q_{omega i}; under the arc, the dotted arc a_i^{omega'} joining the same two end points (left out of the earlier redraw); every stroke ends at the same two end points of the arc. Struck and omitted: the first version below it (Q_{omega i}, R_i^omega, a_i^omega, R_i, crossed out by a zigzag); its right end, the arrow towards Q_{omega' i} labelled (c^{omega'}_{omega' i})^{-1}, is outside the zigzag but belongs to it, and is omitted with it. Left margin: the analogous sketch, three elongated pencil loops drawn as one zigzag stroke, and the short stroke ending in a dot; its small labels (omega, a ...) are not legible and are left out, and the struck squiggle at its top is omitted. Still differs: the label of the left end of the arc is lost in the zigzag and is not drawn; the label Q_{omega i} is placed under the arrowhead, where he wrote it. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

figures.what: left margin: analogous sketch, partly struck

drawings.description: à gauche : sphère portant les trois sommets $Q_0$, $Q_1$, $Q_\infty$ et les six arcs $\tilde a_i^{\pm}$ qui les joignent deux à deux. Légende : $\mathrm{III}_J$.
drawings.kind: sphere with three vertices and six arcs
drawings.notes: Pencil outline (an ellipse); Q_1 (left), Q_infty (middle), Q_0 (right) on the front. Between Q_1 and Q_infty two solid arcs, the upper one tilde a_0^+ and the lower one tilde a_0^- round the left; between Q_infty and Q_0 two solid arcs, the upper one tilde a_1^+ (bulging up to the right edge before coming down to Q_0) and the lower one tilde a_1^-; tilde a_infty^+ dotted over the top from Q_1, and tilde a_infty^- dashed from Q_0 to Q_1 passing just above Q_infty (on the page its two halves meet the solid arcs near Q_infty). Every arc starts and ends at the same vertex points. Still differs: the dotted arc tilde a_infty^+ stops short of Q_0 on the page (at the end, a short tick) and is drawn so; the arrowheads are a reading of overinked strokes (into Q_1 for tilde a_0^+ and tilde a_infty^-, into Q_infty for tilde a_0^- and tilde a_1^+, into Q_0 for tilde a_1^-). Legend III_J and (27) are text, outside the crop. Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: à droite : $Q_{\omega i}$ et $Q_{\omega' i}$ reliés par les deux arcs $\tilde a_i^{\omega}$ (en haut) et $\tilde a_i^{\omega'}$ (en bas) ; au centre, en pointillé, le petit cercle $R_i^{\omega}$, $R_i^{\omega'}$ et l'arc $a_i^{\omega}$.
drawings.kind: two arcs between two vertices around a small circle
drawings.notes: Q_{omega i} (left) and Q_{omega' i} (right) joined by tilde a_i^omega above (arrow to the left) and tilde a_i^{omega'} below (arrow to the right); in the middle, dotted, the small circle through R_i^{omega'}, R_i^omega with the arc a_i^omega, and dotted segments from the Q to the R. The line of text above the figure is not drawn.

drawings.description: sphère : pôles $P_{+}$ (en haut) et $P_{-}$ (en bas) ; sur l'équateur, les sommets $Q_0$, $Q_1$, $Q_\infty$ et les trois points marqués (ronds pleins) ; les arcs $\tilde a_i^{\pm}$ le long de l'équateur, et les méridiens $d_i^{+}$ (de $P_{+}$ à $Q_i$) et $d_i^{-}$ (de $P_{-}$ à $Q_i$), en trait plein ou en pointillé selon qu'ils sont vus ou cachés.
drawings.kind: sphere with poles, meridians and equatorial vertices
drawings.notes: Pencil outline; P^+ above, P_- below; on the equator Q_infty (back left), Q_0 (front), Q_1 (back right) and the three marked points (big dots: left edge, centre, right). Meridians: d_0^+ and d_0^- solid from the poles to Q_0 (arrows into Q_0); d_infty^+-, d_1^+- dashed from the poles to Q_infty and Q_1 (arrows into Q_infty and Q_1). Equatorial arcs, every one between the same vertex points: tilde a_1^+ and tilde a_1^- from Q_0 round the left edge to Q_infty (solid in front, dotted or dashed behind the edge), on either side of the left marked point; tilde a_0^+ and tilde a_0^- dashed between Q_infty and Q_1, on either side of the central point; tilde a_infty^+ and tilde a_infty^- from Q_0 round the right edge to Q_1, on either side of the right marked point. Labels as on the page; the label at the upper left reads tilde a_1^+ (the earlier redraw had tilde a_infty^+ there). Still differs: the label at the upper right edge reads like tilde a_0^+, but the arc it names joins Q_0 and Q_1, so it is set as tilde a_infty^+ (a reading); the sign of the lower middle label tilde a_0^- is hidden; the arrowheads on the equatorial arcs are a reading (into Q_0 for tilde a_1^- and tilde a_infty^+, into Q_1 for tilde a_0^+). The ink blot near Q_infty and the scribbled text above the sphere are not drawn. Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: sphère avec les pôles $P_{+}$, $P_{-}$, les trois points marqués sur l'équateur et les méridiens $d_0^{\pm}$, $d_1^{\pm}$, $d_\infty^{\pm}$. Légende : $\mathrm{V}_J$.
drawings.kind: sphere with poles and meridians
drawings.notes: Pencil outline and equator; P_+ at the top, P_- at the bottom; the front meridian d_0 solid, d_infty and d_1 dashed (hidden); the three marked points on the equator (the left one ringed). Each meridian carries d_i^- above and d_i^+ below, as he labels them. Legend V_J (text) not drawn.

drawings.description: sphère réunissant les figures précédentes : pôles $P^{+}$, $P^{-}$ ; sur l'équateur, $Q_0$, $Q_1$, $Q_\infty$ et, autour de chacun des trois points marqués, le petit cercle $R_i^{\pm}$ avec les arcs $a_i^{\pm}$ ; les arcs $c_i^{\pm}$ joignant les $Q$ aux $R$, et les méridiens $d_i^{\pm}$. Légende : $\mathrm{VI}$.
drawings.kind: sphere with poles, meridians, equatorial vertices and small circles
drawings.notes: Pencil outline; P^+ and P^-; meridians d_0^+- solid from the poles to Q_0, d_infty^+- and d_1^+- dashed from the poles to Q_infty and Q_1 (the hidden d_1^- passing behind the circle round infinity), each with its arrow into the Q; Q_infty, Q_0, Q_1; the three small circles round the marked points, dotted round 0 (top middle), solid round 1 (left) and round infinity (right), each with its two points R^+- on it and its two arcs a^+ (upper half) and a^- (lower half); the arrows c from the Q to the R, each ending at the same R point as its circle: c_infty^- (dashed) from Q_infty to R_0^+, c_infty^+ from Q_infty round the left to R_1^-, c_1^+ (dotted) from Q_1 to R_0^-, c_0^- from Q_0 to R_1^+, c_0^+ from Q_0 to R_infty^-, and the dotted stroke from Q_1 that runs off the right edge (towards R_infty^+, whose label is cut). Still differs: the small arrowheads on the circles are not drawn; the stroke from Q_1 to the right is cut by the edge of the crop; his doubled pencil strokes at the bottom left and bottom right are reduced to one, and the wavy hatching near P^- is not drawn; the small mark above d_infty^+ is left out. Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en bas à gauche : petit triangle $P^{\omega}$, $Q_{\omega i}$, $R_i^{\omega'}$ ; arcs $d^{\omega}_{\omega i}$ de $P^{\omega}$ à $Q_{\omega i}$, $c^{\omega}_{\omega i}$ de $Q_{\omega i}$ à $R_i^{\omega'}$, et le chemin composé $\tilde d_i'^{\omega}$ ; une boucle autour de $R_i^{\omega'}$.
drawings.kind: small path triangle
drawings.notes: P^omega at the top, Q_{omega i} bottom left, R_i^{omega'} bottom right; d^omega_{omega i} from P^omega to Q_{omega i}, c^omega_{omega i} from Q_{omega i} to R_i^{omega'}, the composite tilde d_i'^omega dashed from P^omega to R_i^{omega'}; the loop round R_i^{omega'} is cut by the page edge on the right.

drawings.description: à gauche : $P^{\omega}$ en haut, $Q_{\omega' i}$ en bas, $R_i^{\omega}$ à gauche ; flèche $d^{\omega}_{\omega' i}$ de $P^{\omega}$ à $Q_{\omega' i}$, arc $c^{\omega'}_{\omega' i}$ de $Q_{\omega' i}$ à $R_i^{\omega}$, et en pointillé le chemin composé.
drawings.kind: small path triangle
drawings.notes: P^omega at the top, Q_{omega' i} at the bottom, R_i^omega on the left; d^omega_{omega' i} from P^omega down to Q_{omega' i}, c^{omega'}_{omega' i} from Q_{omega' i} to R_i^omega, the composite path dashed from P^omega to R_i^omega. The number (66) on the right is text.

drawings.description: sphère : les deux pôles, les huit sommets $R_i^{\omega}$, $P^{\omega}$, et les arcs $d_i^{\omega}$, $d_i'^{\omega}$ (méridiens, pleins ou pointillés), $a_i^{\omega}$ (petits cercles) et $b_i^{\omega}$ (le long de l'équateur). Légende : $\mathrm{VII}$.
drawings.kind: sphere with poles, meridians and small circles
drawings.notes: Pencil outline; the two poles, each joined by six meridians to the six vertices on the three small circles of the equator (two vertices per circle, at its left and right ends): to the left and right circles solid, to the middle (hidden) circle dashed; every meridian ends with an arrow at its vertex, and all meridians of a pole start at the same pole point. The three small circles: left (with its marked point) and right in front, each as two solid arcs between its two vertices; the middle one behind, its upper arc dashed and its lower arc solid. Along the equator: the solid arc b between the left and the right circle, the arrow from the left circle out to the left edge, and the dashed back of the equator from the left edge to the middle circle and from the middle circle to the right edge. So 2 poles and 6 vertices: the eight vertices R_i^omega, P^omega of the transcription. No labels on the figure itself (the NB and its text in the left margin are not drawn). Still differs: the arrowheads on the small circles (several, overinked) are not drawn; where the dashed back equator meets the outline is approximate. Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: seconde sphère, au crayon : les deux pôles reliés par trois méridiens, les trois points marqués sur l'équateur. Légende : $\mathrm{VIII} = \mathrm{IV}$.
drawings.kind: sphere with poles and meridians
drawings.notes: All in faint pencil: outline, equator, the two poles joined by three meridians (one in front, two near the outline), the three marked points on the equator. The legend VIII = IV is text, not drawn.

drawings.description: sphère : pôles $P^{+}$, $P^{-}$ ; autour des trois points marqués, les petits cercles $R_i^{\pm}$ avec les arcs $a_i^{\pm}$ ; les méridiens $\tilde d_i^{\pm}$ et $\tilde d_i'^{\pm}$ ($i = 0, 1, \infty$) descendant des pôles vers les $R$, en trait plein ou pointillé selon qu'ils sont vus ou cachés.
drawings.kind: sphere with poles, meridians and small circles
drawings.notes: Crop widened to the right so that the whole sphere is in it (the earlier crop cut the circle round infinity). Pencil outer outline; P^+ and P^-; the three small circles round the marked points (left R_1^-, R_1^+, a_1^+-; middle R_0^+, R_0^-, a_0^+-; right R_infty^-, R_infty^+, a_infty^+-), each with its dot, its two vertices at its left and right ends and its two arcs; the twelve meridians tilde d_i^+-, tilde d_i'^+- from the poles to these vertices, each with its arrow into the vertex and all those of a pole leaving the same pole point: tilde d_0'^+ and tilde d_0'^- dashed, the others solid; the dashed equator (from R_1^- round the left edge to R_0^+, from R_1^+ to R_infty^-, and from R_0^- towards the circle round infinity). Still differs: the arrowheads on the small circles are not drawn; the inked front outline is drawn as the outer meridians tilde d_1'^+ and tilde d_infty^+ only; which inner meridians are dashed is a reading of faint strokes; the label R_infty^+ is cut by the edge of the page, and the blot on tilde d_1^+ near the top is not drawn. Nothing is struck. The legend (VII?) at the bottom right is text. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: une sphère, pôles $P^{+}$ en haut et $P^{-}$ en bas, l'équateur $\Sigma_{\mathbf{R}}$ portant les trois trous $R_0$, $R_1$, $R_\infty$, chacun entouré de son petit cercle $U_i$ marqué des points $R_i^{\pm}$, $S_i^{\pm}$ et des arcs $a_i^{++}, a_i^{+-}, \dots$ ; sur l'équateur les points $Q_0$, $Q_1$, $Q_\infty$ et les arcs orientés $b_i^{\pm}$ ; des pôles partent les méridiens portant les arcs $c_i^{\pm}$ (vers les $Q_i$) et $d_i^{\pm}$ (vers les $S_i$), en traits pleins ou pointillés selon l'hémisphère.
drawings.kind: sphere with poles, meridians, equatorial vertices and holes
drawings.notes: Pencil outline; P^+ and P^-; on the equator Q_1, Q_infty, Q_0 and the three holes, each a small circle U_i round its marked point (U_0 at the left and U_1 at the right in front, U_infty behind in the middle), with its four points R_i^-, S_i^+, R_i^+, S_i^- (left, top, right, bottom). Meridians, every one between the same points: from each pole d_i^+- to the S_i (d_0^+-, d_1^+- solid, d_infty^+- dotted, behind) and c_i^+- to the Q_i (c_infty^+- solid, c_1^+- and c_0^+- dashed); each ends with its arrow. The arcs b along the equator: b_infty^- (from Q_infty to R_0^+, arrow at R_0^+) and b_infty^+ (from Q_infty to R_1^-) solid in front; b_1^- (from Q_1 to R_infty^-) and b_0^+ (from R_infty^+ to Q_0) dotted behind; b_1^+ from Q_1 round the left edge to R_0^- and b_0^- from Q_0 round the right edge to R_1^+, dashed behind and solid in front. Labels: the poles, the Q, the meridians, the b and, round the circles, S_i^+-, R_i^+-, R_i and the legible arcs a. Still differs: the many small labels a_i^{++}, a_i^{+-}, ... and the arrowheads round the circles are overinked; only those read with some confidence are placed (a_0^{++}, a_0^+, a_0^-, a_infty^{++}, a_infty^+, a_infty^-, a_1^{-+}, a_1^{++}, a_1^+, a_1^-), the others are left out; the circle round infinity is drawn whole, solid, though it lies behind. Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: deux sphères en marge. Sur la première, $\widetilde{\Sigma}_\varepsilon$ : $P_\varepsilon$ au sommet, les trois incisions $d$ menant aux points $S_i^{\varepsilon'}$, $S_j^{\varepsilon'}$, $S_k^{\varepsilon'}$ des trous, en trait épais. Sur la seconde, $\widetilde{\Sigma}_i$ : $Q_i$, $Q_j$, $R_i^{\omega}$ et les incisions le long de l'équateur.
drawings.kind: two spheres with incisions
drawings.notes: Top sphere tilde Sigma_epsilon: pencil outline and equator; P_epsilon at the top; the three small circles of the holes on the equator (one behind, two in front); the three incisions in thick strokes, which on the page run from P_epsilon' at the bottom to the points S^{epsilon'} at the bottoms of the circles (the transcription has them from P_epsilon), the one to the back circle dashed; all three start at the same point P_epsilon'. Labels as on the page: S_k^{epsilon'} at the back (middle) circle, S_i^{epsilon'} at the left one, S_j^{epsilon'} at the right one (the earlier redraw had i and k exchanged). Bottom sphere tilde Sigma_i: pencil outline, the pencil lower edge of the equator and the three pencil circles of the holes; the thick incision along the equator from R_k^{omega'} round the left edge through Q_k and tilde R_i^omega, interrupted by the hole of R_i, then on through R_i^omega and Q_j round the right edge down to R_j^omega; the point Q_i below it. Still differs: the label read tilde R_i^omega has a stroke over the R that may be a bar; the label R_i^omega could also be read Q_i^omega; the doubled pencil strokes of both outlines are reduced to one. The captions tilde Sigma_epsilon and tilde Sigma_i stand beside the spheres; the second is cut by the crop and left out. Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): on the page the three thick incisions start from the bottom pole P_epsilon' (the common point is labelled P_epsilon' and P_epsilon is the dot at the top); the redraw stands. Not checked by a reader.
drawings.disagreement: 03-2: on the page the thick incisions of the first sphere start from the bottom pole P_epsilon', not from P_epsilon at the top.

drawings.description: le graphe d'un octaèdre : $P_\varepsilon$ en haut, $P_{\varepsilon'}$ en bas, $Q_i$, $Q_j$, $Q_k$ sur l'équateur, chaque $P$ relié à chaque $Q$.
drawings.kind: triangular bipyramid (octahedron sketch)
drawings.notes: P_epsilon at the top, P_epsilon' at the bottom, Q_i (left), Q_k (right) and Q_j (behind, in the middle) on the equator; each P joined to each Q, and the three equatorial edges Q_i-Q_k, Q_i-Q_j, Q_j-Q_k; every edge drawn between the same five vertex points. Disagreement: with three Q it is the graph of a triangular bipyramid (5 vertices, 9 edges, 6 faces), not of an octahedron as the transcription says. Still differs: the edge P_epsilon-Q_i is doubled on the page (drawn once); the edges Q_i-Q_k and Q_i-Q_j are overdrawn with wavy coil strokes and the edge Q_j-Q_k with a scribble; these strokes are read as crossings-out or emphasis and are not drawn, the edges themselves are drawn plain; the vertical edge Q_j-P_epsilon' is broken where it crosses the front edge, as on the page. Not encoded: the meaning of the wavy strokes is not settled. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): five vertices, P_epsilon, P_epsilon' and three Q, so a triangular bipyramid (the transcription's own list of vertices gives five, an octahedron has six); the label at the right vertex reads Q_j and the one at the middle vertex Q_k (a second, struck label beside it is left out), and the two labels are exchanged accordingly. Not checked by a reader.
drawings.disagreement: 03-3: the graph has five vertices (P_epsilon, P_epsilon', Q_i, Q_j, Q_k): a triangular bipyramid, not an octahedron.

drawings.description: en marge, un petit schéma : $P_\varepsilon$ relié par un lacet $l_0$ au trou $R_{\omega i} \simeq R_0$ (d'orientation $\varpi = \omega \wedge \varepsilon$), au point $Q_\infty$ et au trou $R_{\omega' i} \simeq R_1$.
drawings.kind: small loop diagram between holes
drawings.notes: P_epsilon at the left; the hole R_{omega i} = R_0 at the top right (circle) and the hole R_{omega' i} at the bottom (circle); Q_infty between them. The strokes as on the page: a double stem from P_epsilon to the top circle (the return stroke arrowed towards P_epsilon); from the point B on the lower left of the top circle a stroke down through Q_infty that crosses the next stroke and ends, arrowed, inside the bottom circle; and a double stem from P_epsilon down to the bottom circle, the outer stroke ending on the circle, the inner one (arrowed up, towards P_epsilon) turning right to meet the circle on its upper right. Label l_0 beside the left stem; omega wedge epsilon (varpi = omega wedge epsilon) written along the bottom circle. Disagreement: the label beside the bottom circle reads like simeq R_0 (the transcription has R_{omega' i} simeq R_1); it is set as the transcription reads it. Still differs: the labels are written along the strokes, slanted, on the page (the one of Q, read Q_{omega i} simeq Q_infty, is set slanted); the small marks near the arrowheads are left out. Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): at 600 dpi the label of the bottom hole reads R_{omega i} simeq R_0 (the loop l_0 runs to it) and the label of the top hole R_{omega^2 i} simeq R_1; the point between them reads Q_i simeq Q_infty. The transcription's identifications are right; the earlier redraw had the two holes exchanged, and the labels are corrected (this replaces what the note above says of the top and bottom holes). Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: une sphère : $P_\varepsilon \simeq P_{+}$ au sommet, $P_{\varepsilon'}$ en bas ; le quadrilatère $\widetilde{D}_r$ hachuré entre le méridien de $Q_i \simeq Q_\infty$ et celui du trou $R_{\omega i} \simeq R_1$ ; autour des trous les points $R_{\omega i}^{\omega}$, $S_i^{\varepsilon} \simeq S_0^{\varepsilon}$, $Q_{\omega' i}$ ; légende $r = (i, \omega, \varepsilon)$, $J = \ldots$
drawings.kind: sphere with a hatched quadrilateral
drawings.notes: Crop widened to the right to take in the legend. Pencil outline; P_epsilon = P_+ at the top, P_epsilon' at the bottom. From P_epsilon: the outer meridian down to Q_{omega' i} at the left edge, the meridian to S_i^epsilon = S_0^epsilon at the top of the left hole, the thick vertical arrow to Q_i = Q_infty, and the meridian to S^epsilon_{omega' i} at the top of the right hole; the quadrilateral tilde D_r between the second meridian and the arrow hatched in pencil. The equator in front from Q_{omega' i} round the left hole (its small circle) through Q_i to the right hole (its small circle), the back of the equator in pencil; from the bottom of the left hole and from Q_i the two meridians down to P_epsilon'. Every stroke ends at the same vertex points. Labels round the holes as read: R^omega_{omega i} on both sides of the left hole with simeq R_1 under the right one, S_i^{epsilon'} under it; R^{omega'}_{omega i} and simeq R_1^- at the right hole, R_{omega i} simeq R_1 at its centre. Legend r = (i, omega, epsilon), J = at the right. Still differs: the labels round the left hole are overinked (the hole itself is a blot), their indices are a reading; the label inside the hatched region reads like tilde I_r with a stroke through it, set as tilde D_r as in the transcription; Q_{omega' i} is cut by the left edge of the crop. Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: En haut à gauche, une sphère : pôle nord $P_+$, pôle sud $P_-$ ; sur l'équateur, de gauche à droite, $Q_1$, $R_0^-$, $R_0^+$, $Q_\infty$, $R_1^-$ ; deux petits cercles sur l'équateur, l'un entre $R_0^-$ et $R_0^+$ (avec $S_0^+$ au-dessus, $S_0^-$ au-dessous), l'autre près de $R_1^-$ (avec $S_1^+$) ; des méridiens joignent $P_+$ à $P_-$ ; un fuseau hachuré sous $P_+$, marqué d'une flèche circulaire d'orientation.
drawings.kind: sphere with poles, meridians, small circles and a hatched lune
drawings.notes: Pencil outline; P_+ at the top, P_- at the bottom. From P_+, four inked meridians: the outer one down to Q_1 at the left end of the equator, one to S_0^+ at the top of the small circle round 0, one straight down to Q_infty, one to S_1^+ at the top of the small circle round 1. On the equator, left to right: Q_1, the circle round 0 with R_0^- (left), R_0^+ (right) and S_0^- (bottom), Q_infty, the circle round 1 with R_1^- (lower left); the equator runs from Q_1 to R_0^-, from R_0^+ through Q_infty to R_1^-. From S_0^- and from Q_infty two meridians down to P_-. The lune between the meridians to S_0^+ and to Q_infty is hatched, with the circular orientation arrow in it; the small ring above R_0^+ beside the meridian. Every stroke ends at the same vertex points. Still differs: the doubled pencil strokes (a second, larger pencil circle round 1, a thin second meridian beside the one to Q_infty, faint pencil strokes below the equator) are reduced to the inked ones; the label over the top of the circle round 0 is read S_0^+ (on the page it looks like a + over a small o). Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.notes: In pencil: outline; the small circles round the poles 0 (top, labelled) and infinity (bottom; its label is below the crop and left out), each with four points on it where the paths start or end; the equator, front half solid and back half dashed; four small oriented circles on the equator (drawn, as on the page, as four arcs with arrowheads): front left labelled 1, front middle (i), back middle (i), back right (1). From the four points of the top pole circle, arrowed paths down to the tops of the four circles: to the front ones solid (the one to the left circle inked), to the back ones dashed; from the bottoms of the four circles, paths down to the four points of the bottom pole circle (the one from the back middle circle dashed), each arrowed into its circle. Every path starts and ends at the same points as the circles and pole circles. Still differs: the labels: the front left circle reads 1; the front middle and the back middle circles both carry a small i-like mark (the earlier redraw had the back one unlabelled); the back right one reads like 1 with a flag (the earlier redraw read -1; the transcription has 1, i, -1, -i); they are set as read, with i at both middle circles. The sense of the arrowheads round the small circles is drawn counter-clockwise, a reading of faint strokes; the many thin pencil meridians are left out. The formula 1 -> F_2^2 on the right is text, drawn. Nothing is struck. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): at 600 dpi the circle labels read 1 (front left), i (front middle), -1 (back right; the flag is a minus sign) and -i (back middle, with a short dash before the i), which is the cyclic order of the four points on the equator; the labels of the two back circles are corrected. Not checked by a reader.
